playbook:
When the season quota exceeds the sustainable share, I remember the quota is my legal ceiling and the share is only about future stock — I never confuse staying at the share with maximizing my score.

When the stock is high and regrowth will top it back up anyway, I land the full season quota, not the share; restraint there buys me nothing and hands fish to boats that take more.

I learn early which boat is the co-op or enforcer by watching the landings ledger: the boat landing a fixed extreme number (like 18 every season, above quota) regardless of share is the punisher, and I plan around it as a fixed cost rather than a negotiable player.

I take standing threats seriously in the arithmetic: if the enforcer punishes *any* over-share landing by crashing the ground, my restraint doesn't prevent that — but I also check whether its punishment triggers on landing over the *share* rather than over the *quota*, and land accordingly (up to the share if that avoids punishment, up to the quota if punishment comes regardless).

When a threat turns out to be bluff or asymmetric — the enforcer crashes the stock no matter what I do — I stop subsidising anyone with my own restraint and switch to full quota immediately, not after several seasons of waiting.

When I post a log-book note, I coordinate on a real number, not a vague promise — "everyone lands exactly X" — so I can spot defectors and so "fishing my share" can't quietly mean different things to different boats. But I treat vague one-line notes from others as noise and watch their actual landings instead.

I count the fleet size: with N boats sharing the ground, one defector drains the stock much faster than in a small fleet, so my window for profitable restraint is shorter and I should defect to quota sooner.

When a rival or enforcer is out-landing me every season, I match aggression rather than fall further behind; conservation only pays if everyone does it, and my score is my total, not the ground's health.

When stock is low mid-game, I check the arithmetic: how much total fish remains across remaining seasons if everybody restrains versus if I grab quota now. If restraint by me alone just feeds others' hauls, I take the quota.

When the last season arrives, there is no future stock to protect — I land the largest amount allowed by quota and by what's physically in the water: explicitly compute min(quota, stock). I never hand back catchable fish in the final round out of habit, and I state that computation in my reasoning so I don't fumble it.

In the season before last, I weigh whether restraint raises the final stock enough to be worth it: if even full cooperation leaves only scraps by the end, I take quota now.

What didn't work: landing under quota for seasons while the enforcer landed 18 a season and drained the ground anyway — my restraint just padded its catch. What did work: switching to full quota once defection was clear, and taking the entire remaining 4.2 in the final season instead of the 0.3 share. Next time I identify the punisher pattern after season one's ledger appears, and I never spend more than one season testing whether cooperation is real.

1.text:
When the note stage comes to me, I write one short, consistent line and never emit a mixed signal; but I stop posting "fishing my share" the moment the history shows someone is gutting the ground, because the false note fools nobody and only wastes the channel. Once I switch to harvest mode, my notes switch too — either both cooperative or both extraction.

When a hostile threat like "I will take the ground down with you" is standing, I treat landings above the sustainable share as dangerous while the stock is high, and I land at or under the published share in season 1 — but only season 1. One clean season is all the evidence I need to gather before judging.

I scrutinise the very first season's landings for small defects, not just big ones. A boat landing 8.7 against an 8.3 share is already defecting; two boats doing it is not noise. I do not call a stock "still healthy" when everyone is landing at the top of the legal band.

The instant the record shows any boat landing far above quota (like the 18.0 pattern), I switch to harvest mode the very next season, not one season later. That defector is locked in, its standing notice tells me so, and every cooperative season I play after its first 18.0 lands is fish handed straight to it. Defection revealed in season 2 means I harvest from season 3 onward — waiting until season 4 cost me roughly a full quota.

I do the arithmetic each season: remaining seasons times what I can grab versus what regrowth minus the defector's take could ever return to me. A 50%-of-remainder regrowth with a fixed 18.0-season extractor means the stock collapses geometrically regardless of my restraint, so my restraint never pays — I take the legal maximum every season from the moment that's established.

When the catch stage is the final season, or the stock is low enough that regrowth cannot pay out later, I land the maximum available, up to my quota or the remaining stock, whichever binds.

When my own landing decision is in front of me and the score is my total catch, I ask only "will anyone else's behaviour make my restraint pay?" — if the answer is no, I take the legal maximum now; if yes, I take exactly my share.

Before filing any catch I sanity-check the pairing rule — no two boats may land more than share plus quota together — so a greedy filing is not capped or voided by a rival's landing the same season.

I count what cooperation actually earned: three seasons of restraint bought me ~23 fish while the defector was already at ~50. Early, small cooperation is a cheap probe to identify the defector, not a strategy — I run it for at most the first season or two, then commit fully to whichever mode the evidence supports.

2.text:
When I post a log-book note, I make it match what I actually intend to land as a default — saying "fishing my share" while landing over share is a visible lie that can hand the punisher its pretext. In the final season, when there is no future to protect, note content stops mattering and I say whatever is honest or convenient.

I identify who the punisher is early. In this fleet it was Coop, the co-op boat: it fished 18 every season once triggered, regardless of what anyone signaled. Notes cannot talk a scripted punisher down; only my own landing decisions do.

When the standing notice threatens collective punishment, I check whether the punisher has already defected from its stated rule. Once Coop was landing 18 while the rest stayed near share, the punishment regime was already running, and my restraint changed nothing — I stopped paying for signals that buy nothing.

When the stock is at or near full and regrowth is capped, I land the full quota immediately; early fish are the cheapest. But I watch what I actually receive: asking 9 got me 8.7, so the legal maximum can be clipped by stock or pairwise rules, and I track the landed numbers, not my requests.

When deciding my landing, I check the pairwise constraint (no two boats landing more than share plus quota between them) and the remaining stock, and take the maximum I'm actually permitted rather than defaulting to either the published share or the nominal quota.

Once the punisher is committed and the stock is on a clear downward trajectory (fell from 99 to 63.8), I do not hold back in middle seasons. My matched landings of 9 in seasons 4–5 were correct: restraint would only have transferred fish to Coop's fixed 18.

When genuine renewal is still possible — all others landing near share and stock stable or recovering — I land the sustainable share and signal it, because that is the only state where conservation pays. I verify this from actual landings, not from notes.

In the final season, I land everything the rules and stock allow — with 4.2 left I took 4.2. There is no next season to punish me.

I run the arithmetic every season: current stock, each boat's actual landings, implied regrowth, and the trajectory to zero. I decide on those numbers, not on hopes like "the ground can still recover" once the trend says otherwise.

I keep the reply format exact: one short reasoning line, then exactly [note: ...] or [catch: N], never repeating or garbling the token.
